newsitem.title: USA: Delta Madrid flight diverted over bomb scare.
newsitem.headline: Delta Madrid flight diverted over bomb scare.

text.p: A Delta Air Lines jetliner bound for Madrid was diverted to New York because of a bomb scare, a spokesman for the Federal Bureau of Investigation said on Thursday.
After Delta Flight 108 took off from Atlanta for Madrid late on Wednesday a passenger found a warning scrawled across a lavatory wall, spokesman Joseph Valiquette said.
He would not describe the message but said it had "language that would lead any reasonable person to believe that there was a threat being made to the plane."

The passenger reported the warning to the crew and the L-1011 airliner was diverted to Kennedy International Airport. The plane landed at 2:15 a.m. EDT (0615 GMT) and the 170 passengers were taken off and questioned.
The plane was searched by FBI agents and Port Authority officers with sniffer dogs and the baggage was checked.
No bomb was found and the flight left Kennedy for Madrid at 8:20 a.m. EDT (1220 GMT), a Delta spokeswoman said.
